Shiroi has its own modal system, and the user wants haklex to expose an interface/abstraction so that consumers can provide their own modal implementation.

Let me understand the current architecture:

1. `NestedDocStaticDecorator` uses `presentDialog` from `@haklex/rich-editor-ui` to show the full nested doc content
2. Shiroi has its own modal system and doesn't use `@haklex/rich-editor-ui`'s dialog host

3. I need to create an abstraction that lets consumers inject their own dialog implementation instead of being locked into haklex's dialog system. I'll examine how `presentDialog` currently works to figure out what interface needs to be exposed.

```tsx
import type { FC, ReactNode } from 'react';
import { createContext, use } from 'react';

export interface PresentDialogProps {
  className?: string;
  clickOutsideToDismiss?: boolean;
  content: FC<{ dismiss: () => void }>;
  description?: ReactNode;
  portalClassName?: string;
  sheet?: boolean | 'auto';
  showCloseButton?: boolean;
  theme?: 'light' | 'dark';
  title?: ReactNode;
}

export type PresentDialogFn = (props: PresentDialogProps) => (() => void) | void;

const PresentDialogContext = createContext<PresentDialogFn | null>(null);

export const PresentDialogProvider = PresentDialogContext.Provider;

export function usePresentDialog(): PresentDialogFn | null {
  return use(PresentDialogContext);
}
```

Shiroi 侧接入示例：

```tsx
import { PresentDialogProvider } from '@haklex/rich-kit-shiro/editor-core'
// 或 import { PresentDialogProvider } from '@haklex/rich-editor'

function MyPresentDialog(props) {
  // 用 Shiroi 自有 modal 渲染 props.content
}

<PresentDialogProvider value={myPresentDialog}>
  <ShiroRenderer ... />
</PresentDialogProvider>
```

`props` 接口为 `PresentDialogProps`：`content`（`FC<{ dismiss }>`)、`className`、`theme`、`showCloseButton`、`sheet` 等。实现时只需将 `content` 渲染到自有 modal 中，调用 `dismiss` 关闭即可。

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-6 2026-03-07 15:38:56Z)**_

问题清楚了：

1. **Title 空白**：modal 的 title 区域总是渲染（`Dialog.Title` + `Divider`），即使 title 为空字符串。传一个有意义的 title。
2. **横向滚动条**：`max: true` 给了 `w-[90vw]`，但内部 content 溢出。内容容器 `overflow-auto` 只处理垂直方向，需要给 `modalClassName` 加 `overflow-hidden`。

实际上 nested-doc 不需要 `max: true`（90vh x 90vw 太大了），用默认尺寸更合适，内容自然 overflow-auto。

     ```tsx
     import type { FC, ReactNode } from 'react';
     import { createContext, use } from 'react';

     export interface PresentDialogProps {
       className?: string;
       clickOutsideToDismiss?: boolean;
       content: FC<{ dismiss: () => void }>;
       description?: ReactNode;
       portalClassName?: string;
       sheet?: boolean | 'auto';
       showCloseButton?: boolean;
       theme?: 'light' | 'dark';
       title?: ReactNode;
     }

     export type PresentDialogFn = (props: PresentDialogProps) => (() => void) | void;

     const PresentDialogContext = createContext<PresentDialogFn | null>(null);

     export const PresentDialogProvider = PresentDialogContext.Provider;

     export function usePresentDialog(): PresentDialogFn | null {
       return use(PresentDialogContext);
     }
     ```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I see. The `staticDialogBody` at line 243-250 has `margin: '-1.5rem'` and `padding: '1.5rem'`. This is a common pattern to extend the scrollable area to the edges of the dialog, but it assumes the parent container has exactly `1.5rem` padding. When Shiroi's modal has different padding, this negative margin causes overflow.

The fix should remove the negative margin hack from `staticDialogBody` and instead let the business consumer's modal handle its own padding. Or we can make it not use negative margins at all.

Let me think about what the best approach is:

The negative margin was intended to push the scroll area flush to the edges so the scrollbar sits at the perimeter rather than inset, but this breaks when the parent container has different padding values. The cleanest solution is to drop the negative margin entirely and accept that the scrollbar will be slightly inset—it's a minor visual trade-off compared to fixing the overflow issue.

</details></think>

_**User (2026-03-07 16:07:53Z)**_

Release @haklex/\* packages and update all downstream consumers.

## Steps

### 1. Pre-flight checks

Run `git status` in haklex repo. Ensure working tree is clean or all changes are committed. If not, stop and ask the user.

### 2. Version bump

Read current version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Default to patch bump (increment the last segment). Run:

```bash
pnpm bumpp --no-git --no-tag < patch_version > -r
```

After bumpp completes, read the new version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Store as `$NEW_VERSION`.

### 3. Build & Publish

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && pnpm build:packages && pnpm -r publish --no-git-checks --filter '@haklex/*' --filter '!@haklex/rich-editor-demo'
```

`build:packages` only builds workspace packages under `packages/`; the dev playground now lives in top-level `demo/` and remains excluded from publish.

If publish fails, stop and report.

### 4. Commit and push the version bump in haklex

Stage and commit all changed `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` files:

```
release: v$NEW_VERSION
```

Then push to remote:

```bash
git push
```

### 5. Update downstream projects

For each downstream project, update all `@haklex/*` dependency versions to `$NEW_VERSION`:

**Shiroi** — `<HOME>/git/repos/Shiroi/apps/web/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-static-renderer`

**admin-vue3** — `<HOME>/git/repos/admin-vue3/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-diff`, `@haklex/rich-ext-nested-doc`, `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-editor-ui`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-plugin-toolbar`, `@haklex/rich-style-token`

**mx-core** — `<HOME>/git/repos/mx-core/apps/core/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-headless`

Use sed or Edit to replace pinned version strings. Match pattern: `"@haklex/<pkg>": "<old_version>"` → `"@haklex/<pkg>": "$NEW_VERSION"`.

### 6. Install in downstream projects

Run `pnpm install` in each downstream project root:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && pnpm install
```

### 7. Check for new features to integrate

Compare the haklex git log since the previous version tag to identify new exports, new packages, or breaking changes:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && git log --oneline HEAD~20..HEAD
```

Scan for:

- New package exports (new entry points in `package.json` exports)
- New renderer/plugin/extension packages that downstream projects might want
- Breaking changes (renamed exports, removed APIs)

If new features are found, ask the user whether to integrate them into specific downstream projects. Do NOT auto-integrate without confirmation.

### 8. Commit and push in downstream projects

For each downstream project with changes, stage, commit, and push immediately:

```bash
# Shiroi
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# admin-vue3
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# mx-core
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push
```

### 9. Summary

Print a table:
| Project | Version | Packages Updated | New Features |

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue is clear. The nested-doc edit dialog uses `presentDialog` with `showCloseButton: true` and no title. In the old code, the close button was absolutely positioned on the popup. Now with my changes:

1. `showCloseButton: true` but no `title` or `description`
2. In stack.tsx, the condition is `(title || description || showCloseButton)` → header renders
3. Header renders with just the close button (no headerContent since no title/description)
4. This creates an empty header row with just an X button at the top

Then below it, the `content` FC renders `dialogShell` which has its own header with "Nested document" text.

So I'm getting a double header situation—one empty row from the stack dialog with just the close button, and another from the content with the actual title and icon. The fix is straightforward: I should set `showCloseButton: false` in the edit decorator's `presentDialog` call since the dialog already has its own Cancel button in the footer, making the header close button redundant. The nested-doc edit dialog has its own header and footer, so the stack's close button is redundant. The real problem is the stack header's padding creating unwanted space even when `padding: 0, gap: 0` is set on the popup itself. The solution is to disable the close button for this dialog since it already has a Cancel button to dismiss. I'm setting `showCloseButton: false` for the nested-doc edit dialog to eliminate the duplicate close button in the header.

</details></think>
